```text
{"language": "en", "title": "Ask the child to explain her steps", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}

<module>
[purpose] What this does

[materials] What you need
```

## PV-HEARD:show_bundles (en)

hash `147d91b55e13c993`, 882 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Show it with bundles of ten', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Show it with bundles of ten", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
The teacher builds the number with bundles of ten sticks and loose sticks, so the child sees tens and ones as things she can hold.

[materials] What you need
Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks, a cloth or mat

[steps] Steps
Build the number with bundles and loose sticks.
Ask the child to say how many tens and how many ones.
Do the sum with the sticks, then write it.

[example] An example
Say sixty-two. Build it with 6 bundles and 2 loose sticks, then ask the child to write what she built.

[check] How to know it worked
Say "sixty-two" to three children, one at a time, and ask each to write it. Then ask each to build it with bundles and say how many bundles and loose sticks. Notice who writes 602.
</module>
```

## ADD-NOCARRY:show_bundles (en)

hash `567b1bc8eb3f171a`, 885 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Show it with bundles of ten', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
{"language": "en", "title": "Show it with bundles of ten", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
```

```text
எத்தனை பத்துகள், எத்தனை ஒன்றுகள் என்று குழந்தையைச் சொல்லச் சொல்லுங்கள்.

ஒன்றுகளின் கூட்டுத்தொகை பத்துக்கு மேல் வரும் ஒரு கூட்டல் கணக்கைக் கொடுங்கள். கட்டுகளையும் குச்சிகளையும் வைத்துக் கூட்டச் சொல்லுங்கள். பத்துத் தனிக்குச்சிகளை ஒரு புதிய கட்டாகக் கட்டுகிறதா என்று கவனியுங்கள்.
```

## ADD-NOCARRY:check_back (en)

hash `16e2bc882d663b36`, 730 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Check by adding back', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Check by adding back", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
After a subtraction, add the answer to the smaller number. It must give the bigger number. A dropped borrow shows up at once.

[materials] What you need
Slate or notebook

[steps] Steps
Add the answer to the number taken away.
It must give the first number back.
If it does not, find the step that changed it.

[example] An example
72 - 38 = 34, check: 34 + 38 = 72.

[check] How to know it worked
Give one addition where the ones add to more than ten. Ask the child to add it with bundles and sticks. Notice whether she ties ten loose sticks into a new bundle.
</module>
```

## SUB-SFL:ask_explain (en)

hash `c63680af354abf88`, 827 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Ask the child to explain her steps', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Ask the child to explain her steps", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
The teacher asks "How did you get that?" and listens before saying whether it is right.

[materials] What you need
No materials needed.

[steps] Steps
Ask "How did you get that?"
Listen all the way through before saying whether it is right.
Ask her to show the same step with sticks.

[example] An example
A child wrote 47 for 62 - 29, which is the mistake. Ask: how did you get 47? The child says: 9 minus 2 is 7, and 6 minus 2 is 4.

[check] How to know it worked
Write a subtraction where the ones digit on top is smaller. Ask one child "is 2 take away 6 the same as 6 take away 2?" and listen. Then ask her to do the whole sum with bundles.
</module>
```

## SUB-SFL:show_bundles (en)

```text
Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks, a cloth or mat
```

## SUB-SFL:decomposition (en)

hash `74f61435a47544a4`, 804 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Subtract in parts (decomposition)', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Subtract in parts (decomposition)", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
Subtract the tens, then the ones, bridging through a ten, shown with bundles.

[materials] What you need
Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks

[steps] Steps
Take away the tens first.
Take away the ones in two steps, through the next ten.
Say the whole sum aloud at the end.

[example] An example
63 - 28: take away 2 bundles (63 - 20 = 43), then 8 sticks in two steps: 3 to reach 40, then 5 more, so 63 - 28 = 35.

[check] How to know it worked
Write a subtraction where the ones digit on top is smaller. Ask one child "is 2 take away 6 the same as 6 take away 2?" and listen. Then ask her to do the whole sum with bundles.
</module>
```

## SUB-SFL:exchange_ten (en)

hash `2d8875a168d11150`, 854 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Open a bundle to get ten loose sticks', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text

{"language": "en", "title": "Open a bundle to get ten loose sticks", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
When there are not enough loose sticks to take away, the teacher opens one bundle. One bundle fewer, ten more loose sticks.

[materials] What you need
Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks

[steps] Steps
Build the top number.
Ask "can I take this many from the loose sticks?"
If not, open one bundle into ten loose sticks and count again.

[example] An example
91 - 56 = 35: 1 loose stick is too few to take 6; open a bundle, now 11 loose sticks and 8 bundles.

[check] How to know it worked
Write a subtraction where the ones digit on top is smaller. Ask one child "is 2 take away 6 the same as 6 take away 2?" and listen. Then ask her to do the whole sum with bundles.
</module>
```

```text
[purpose] What this does
For a number close to a ten, subtract the ten, then give back what was taken too much.
```

```text
</module>
```

## SUB-SFL:check_back (en)

hash `3eb4551e0704b8b1`, 745 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Check by adding back', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Check by adding back", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
After a subtraction, add the answer to the smaller number. It must give the bigger number. A dropped borrow shows up at once.

[materials] What you need
Slate or notebook

[steps] Steps
Add the answer to the number taken away.
It must give the first number back.
If it does not, find the step that changed it.

[example] An example
72 - 38 = 34, check: 34 + 38 = 72.

[check] How to know it worked
Write a subtraction where the ones digit on top is smaller. Ask one child "is 2 take away 6 the same as 6 take away 2?" and listen. Then ask her to do the whole sum with bundles.
```

## SUB-NODEC:ask_explain (en)

hash `fb395e4787a7f891`, 801 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Ask the child to explain her steps', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text

{"language": "en", "title": "Ask the child to explain her steps", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
The teacher asks "How did you get that?" and listens before saying whether it is right.

[materials] What you need
No materials needed.

[steps] Steps
Ask "How did you get that?"
Listen all the way through before saying whether it is right.
Ask her to show the same step with sticks.

[example] An example
A child wrote 44 for 72 - 38, which is the mistake. Ask: how did you get 44? The child says: I took a ten for the 2, then took 3 from 7.

[check] How to know it worked
Give one subtraction that needs borrowing. Ask the child to show it with bundles and tell you what happens to the tens after she opens a bundle.
</module>
```

## SUB-NODEC:decomposition (en)

hash `e9e1d7f8252caf75`, 770 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Subtract in parts (decomposition)', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 3}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Subtract in parts (decomposition)", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 3}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
Subtract the tens, then the ones, bridging through a ten, shown with bundles.

[materials] What you need
Bundles of ten sticks, loose sticks

[steps] Steps
Take away the tens first.
Take away the ones in two steps, through the next ten.
Say the whole sum aloud at the end.

[example] An example
63 - 28: take away 2 bundles (63 - 20 = 43), then 8 sticks in two steps: 3 to reach 40, then 5 more, so 63 - 28 = 35.

[check] How to know it worked
Give one subtraction that needs borrowing. Ask the child to show it with bundles and tell you what happens to the tens after she opens a bundle.
</module>
```

## SUB-NODEC:compensation (en)

hash `4159dc0452770692`, 730 characters, facts `{'language': 'en', 'title': 'Subtract a nearby ten, then adjust (compensation)', 'module_number': 1, 'module_count': 3, 'step_count': 2}`

```text
<facts>
{"language": "en", "title": "Subtract a nearby ten, then adjust (compensation)", "module_number": 1, "module_count": 3, "step_count": 2}
</facts>
<module>
[purpose] What this does
For a number close to a ten, subtract the ten, then give back what was taken too much.

[materials] What you need
A number line drawn on the ground or slate

[steps] Steps
Choose a number close to a ten.
Take away the ten, then give back what you took too much.

[example] An example
63 - 29: take away 30 (63 - 30 = 33), then give 1 back, so 63 - 29 = 34.

[check] How to know it worked
Give one subtraction that needs borrowing. Ask the child to show it with bundles and tell you what happens to the tens after she opens a bundle.
</module>
```
